newsitem.title: USA: Maystadt sees IMF accord on capital movements.
newsitem.headline: Maystadt sees IMF accord on capital movements.

text.p: International Monetary Fund members are likely to agree to a change to the IMF's statutes to give it a mandate to push for full liberalisation of capital movements, Philippe Maystadt, head of the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee said on Saturday.

"There is an agreement on the broad principle that capital movement liberalisation is beneficial and the Fund could have a useful role in promoting free capital movements," he said ahead of full ministerial meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
"I think we will be able to confirm agreement on an extension of the (IMF's) jurisdiction," Maystadt, who is also Belgium's finance minister, said.
The IMF already encourages its members to liberalise capital flows, but has no official mandate to do so.

Maystadt said there would have to be recognition among IMF members that there might have to be "transitional arrangements" in some countries to ensure that full liberalisation of capital movements was accompanied by economic reforms.

He declined to say what these transitional arrangements would be, though IMF officials have suggested previously that the Fund might have to provide money in the short term to help countries through any instability caused by liberalisation.
Maystadt said a system would also have to be put in place to allow members to impose temporary restrictions on both capital inflows and outflows when necessary, if this were approved by the IMF.
The IMF's Interim Committee meets on Monday.
